T ECHNICAL OVERVIEW In this section, we begin by describing our hard instance and provide a complete proof of a lower bound against Krylov Iteration (Algorithm 13) for Spectral LRA. We then outline the approach to establish a lower bound against Block Krylov and explain how to lift a lower bound against Block Krylov to a general matrix-vector product lower bound. Finally, we discuss the new ideas we require to obtain a better upper bound for Schatten-p LRA, when p is a fixed constant. A. statement: Remark 7 (Krylov Iteration vs. Block Krylov). Bakshi, Clarkson and Woodruff run two instantiations of Krylov methods in parallel, one with block size 1 and another with block size O(1/ε1/3 ). Combined with our lower bounds, our results imply that we never need to run Krylov iteration with a block size larger than 1 for rank-1 low-rank approximation. While we focus on the rank-1 case, we note that our upper bound techniques for obtaining a Schatten-p rank-1 LRA approximation with Õ(1/ε1/3 ) queries can be used to obtain a Schatten-p rank-k LRA approximation using O(k log(k/ε)/ε1/3 ) queries. This slightly improves over the O(k log n/ε1/3 )-query algorithm and analysis of [5], as we remove any dependence on the full dimension n. However, rather than only using a single starting vector, we apply a method more similar to that of [5], which requires Block Krylov with two different block sizes. A natural question that we leave open is whether we need to combine two different block sizes.
